messages:
maria: Noticed a sustained IOPS spike on a subset of eu-west1 scratch hosts since ~04:10 UTC. GPU attaches delayed ~2-6m, pod Pending count up.
jonathan: Alert triggered: `scratch.nvme.write_amp > 6` for 28m on eu-west1-b cohort. Attach success rate down ~35%.
lee: Any SMART/dmesg hints?
sree: Found repeated `blk_update_request: I/O error` on 3 hosts. Scrub backlog climbing, temp and SMART counters look fine. Appears to be tiny-write churn + janitor overlap.
maria: Can we throttle janitor for that cohort? Also avoid scheduling new GPU attaches to those hosts.
jonathan: Pushing janitor config change: concurrency 10 -> 1 for affected affinity pool. Rolling now.
lee: I'll cordon/taint the hot nodes to force scheduler to fallback. Quick one-off:
```
kubectl cordon euw-node-123
kubectl taint nodes euw-node-123 scratch-io=hot:NoSchedule
```
deploy-bot: routing override applied: `gpu.provision.region_preference = [us-west1, eu-west1]` for new allocations. ETA ~30s. :white_check_mark:
maria: Note: cross-region routing may increase cost by ~12% and latency for EU customers for ~2h. Ops okay with that for mitigation?
jonathan: Agreed. CS notified if >1% of attaches affected.
lee: After taint, 4/5 stuck pods rescheduled within 90s. Attach queue length falling.
sree: Filing RFC for longer-term fixes: write-merge window (coalesce tiny writes 50ms), hot-reservation pool, and janitor backoff heuristics. Link: https://go/repo/rfc/scratch-hot-pool (placeholder).
maria: I'll post a short summary to #incidents and tag CS. Will update when scrub backlog drops and attach metrics recover. :thumbsup:
